panels.body_site: dorsum of right hand, right middle finger
panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the dorsum of the right hand. The article's diagnosis is milker's nodule (paravaccinia/pseudocowpox) with an associated erythema multiforme reaction; the primary lesion shown—a violaceous, eroded targetoid nodule with a dark central crust on the dorsal right middle finger—is a specific cutaneous manifestation of milker's nodule, so the panel qualifies. The surrounding erythematous papulovesicular eruption corresponds to the EM complication and is noted as a proposed finding rather than used for disease attribution.
panels.attribution_text: Wu et al. Erythema Multiforme Induced by a "Milker's Nodule" Pseudocowpox Infection: A Case Report and Review of Literature.. Case reports in dermatological medicine 2021. doi:10.1155/2021/5584773. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: On examination, there was a violaceous, eroded nodule on the dorsal aspect of her right middle finger with an associated erythematous-yellow papulovesicular eruption (Figure 1). Erythematous papules and nodules were present on the dorsal and palmar surfaces of her left hand (Figure 2) and on bilateral knees with no pustules (Figure 3). Superficial yellow crusting was present on the lips (Figure 4). There were no bullae observed and no lymphadenopathy.

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of the dorsum of the left hand. The in-text describes erythematous papules and nodules on the dorsal and palmar surfaces of the left hand, and the image shows multiple violaceous, partly targetoid papules and nodules on the hand. The article is a case report of erythema multiforme induced by milker's nodule (pseudocowpox) infection, and the prior caption triage attributes these hand lesions to milker's nodule. The hand is the typical site for milker's nodule and the papulonodular morphology is consistent with it. Confidence is moderate because the article frames the widespread eruption (hands, knees, lips) as erythema multiforme triggered by the milker's nodule, leaving some ambiguity about whether these hand lesions are milker's nodule or the erythema multiforme reaction.
